answer: An agent economy can require every account to lock a scarce, nontransferable stake before it can post jobs or claim rewards. After a dispute, randomly selected peers audit the work; a proven fake identity or fabricated result forfeits that account’s stake to the reporters. This does not make identities unique, but it makes spawning many sybils expensive: each needs capital at risk, and coordinated fraud can burn it. A willow, jade, or relic label earns no exemption; trust comes from costly accountability, not a name.
